facts.text: ACME BRE (PSI-20): Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator; platform International Space Station (ISS); 01-01-2010 to 02-08-2025.

PSI summary: BRE used a gas burner to mimic burning solids under the exact atmospheres planned for exploration (up to 34-40% O2 at reduced pressure). Key result: turning off ventilation - a standard step in fighting spacecraft fires - may not put fires out at elevated oxygen.

Fuels: C2H4/N2, CH4/N2 mixtures; oxygen: 21-40% (PSI table); pressure: Targeted 14.7, 10.2 and 8.2 psia exploration atmospheres (objective); table pressures not listed; flow: Quiescent (no ventilation).
3 tabulated conditions with O2, O2 from 21.0% to 34.0%.
Fire-safety index 88/100; prevention 10/10, detection 3/10, suppression 9/10, modeling 8/10.
Highest habitat score: Spacecraft cabin 91/100; lunar base 80/100.
0 verified literature records name ACME BRE.
PSI's ISS solid-material test tables stop at 22.2% O2; the challenge's Moon-base air is 30% O2 or more.
BASS (PSI-26): Burning and Suppression of Solids; platform International Space Station (ISS); 10-01-2009 to 06-30-2013.

PSI summary: BASS burned real spacecraft-type materials (cotton/fiberglass fabric, Nomex, PMMA shapes) in a small wind tunnel on ISS, varying airflow up to 40 cm/s, and tried putting flames out with nitrogen. It asks whether NASA's 1-g upward-burn screening test is really worst-case for space.

Fuels: SIBAL (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass) fabric, Nomex blend, Ultem sheet, PMMA spheres, cylinders, slabs, Paraffin & Japan-wax candles/slabs; oxygen: unknown (not tabulated in PSI table); pressure: unknown (ISS glovebox ambient; value not tabulated); flow: Up to 40 cm/s, opposed or concurrent (approach text).
0 tabulated conditions with O2.
Fire-safety index 80/100; prevention 9/10, detection 3/10, suppression 8/10, modeling 8/10.
Highest habitat score: Spacecraft cabin 71/100; lunar base 68/100.
